title: PRD: Convert incident heatmap and operator runbook actions into staged delivery gates, synthetic checks, and rollback thresholds
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: A recent regional KV-cache incident (see linked postmortem) surfaced a set of operator runbook steps and mitigation actions that we now need to bake directly into the product requirements so future rollouts and model/kernel changes carry measurable, executable safety checks. Goal: produce a PRD update that maps postmortem action items into three concrete engineering deliverables: staged delivery gates with pass/fail criteria, synthetic and canary checks that run automatically at rollout and on demand, and clear rollback/trip thresholds tied to SLO degradation. The PRD should give engineering the acceptance criteria and observability hooks required for implementation and verification by QA and SRE teams.
scope: In-scope: PRD text, acceptance tests, synthetic check definitions, rollout gate thresholds, runbook-triggered automated verification, links to dashboards and alert rules. Out-of-scope: actual runtime kernel changes, provisioning of extra GPUs for warm pool (these are separate ENG tickets), and customer-facing status messaging templates (handled by comms).
assumptions: We have an existing incident postmortem with action items assigned to engineering and SRE
SRE owns synthetic runner and alerting infra; PM owns acceptance criteria and verification matrix
Rollouts will use current canary/circuit-breaker plumbing in runtime-1.24
acceptance_criteria: A structured PRD section exists that lists each postmortem action item and the exact delivery gate that enforces it (gate name, metric, pass/fail threshold, measurement window)
For every gate, there is at least one synthetic test that can be executed in CI and on-demand in staging (test definition, expected output, failure mode)
Rollout policy includes automated rollback triggers that map to SLO tiers: e.g., if 99th-tail latency increases by >40% over baseline for 5m across canary traffic, rollout halts and reverts
Observable metrics and dashboards are referenced by ID and contain token-level breakdown and tail-latency histograms required by the gate
QA checklist and a small suite of reproducible traffic scenarios (prefix-heavy KV-cache regen, burst cold starts, large-embedding rerun) are attached to the PRD
Owners and on-call contacts for gate failures are specified and aligned with runbook steps in the incident postmortem
deliverables: PRD section: 'Incident-derived gates and synthetic checks' (documented and reviewed)
Acceptance test matrix (spreadsheet) with links to synthetic runners and data sets
Template rollout policy with parametric thresholds (can be consumed by rollout orchestrator)
Verification plan for release engineering and SRE signoff
outcomes: Reduced time-to-detect regressions during model/kernel rollouts
Automated halt-and-rollback behavior for critical SLO regressions
Clear product requirements that reduce ambiguity for engineering and SRE implementation
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and QA to align on postmortem items to be encoded. Action: PM to map top-7 action items into candidate gates (Aisha).
2026-03-04: Runtime engineering clarified that prefix/KV-cache stall is measurable via existing kv_cache_regen_latency and cache_miss_ratio metrics. Added as primary gate signals.
2026-03-06: Decided to use two measurement windows: 5m short-term for rapid rollback triggers and 1h for degraded-state alerts. Drafted threshold proposals attached.
2026-03-08: SRE requested that synthetic checks include deterministic replay traffic (stored seed + prompt set). PM to add examples and storage location to PRD.
2026-03-10: Product review scheduled 2026-03-15. Blocker: need a dashboard link with token-level tail-latency histograms; ENG assigned ENG-22178 to add visualization.
risks: False positives from synthetic checks can unnecessarily block rollouts — requires careful calibration and a muted initial rollout window
Insufficient historical baselines may make percentage thresholds noisy for low-volume models on Dedicated capacity
Ownership ambiguity between Runtime and SRE for synthetic runner maintenance could delay verification
mitigations: Phase 1: conservative thresholds with manual gating for first two releases; Phase 2: automated enforcement after calibration
Require minimum data volume before applying percentage-based thresholds; fallback to absolute-value thresholds when volume below threshold
Add explicit owner rows in PRD and update team runbooks to clarify synthetic runner ownership
next_steps: SRE to provision deterministic replay dataset and store path by 2026-03-12 (Seth)
Run a mock canary with synthetic checks in staging and record results (QA) before 2026-03-20
Schedule cross-team signoff meeting to approve thresholds and verification plan: target 2026-03-15
